documents.title: Academic Integrity Guidelines for AI Use
documents.summary: Landing page of the Honor Code Council's AI guidance. It says the university has no AI policy, leaves the decision to instructors, and urges them to spell out expectations, pointing to faculty-success, information-security and Honor Code Council resources.
documents.stance_why: The page says Texas State "does not have a policy regarding the use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the classroom" and gives instructors "the academic freedom to determine appropriate use", so it sets no stance itself and hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: The page says the university has no AI policy and that this gives instructors "the academic freedom to determine appropriate use for their own courses". The decision is placed with each instructor, which is P04, not a default stance.

documents.stance_why: The guidelines say the university "supports responsible experimentation and use of AI tools" and that "these guidelines are not new University policy". On coursework they say only that "faculty should be clear with students" about permitted uses, so they set no stance and defer to instructors.
